minigame.oxygen-factory.guide1: Mars air is CO₂. You can't breathe it! But it has oxygen (O) inside.
minigame.oxygen-factory.guide2: MOXIE, a NASA machine that went to Mars, heats the CO₂ and takes one O out.
minigame.oxygen-factory.guide3: Inside MOXIE, two O stick together and make O₂. That's why it needs 2 CO₂!
minigame.oxygen-factory.guide4: O₂ is the oxygen we breathe! It goes to the tank.
minigame.oxygen-factory.introTitle: How do we make oxygen on Mars?
cabin.message.title: Message from your guide
cabin.welcome.arrival: Welcome aboard! Look out the window: we are arriving at Mars.
cabin.welcome.context: Mars is a cold world with a very thin atmosphere.
cabin.welcome.simulation: In this simulation, you will run a base and look after its crew.
cabin.welcome.bars: Oxygen, food, shield and energy: all four bars count!
cabin.welcome.preparation: Before landing, open the mission manual.
cabin.manualDone: All set! Tap the center screen to choose where to land.
cabin.again: Hi again! Tap the center screen to choose a destination.
cabin.manualFirst: First open the mission manual: it is the tablet.
manual.mission.title: Your mission
manual.mission.text: You will run a base on Mars for {sols} sols. A sol is a Martian day: it lasts 24 hours and 39 minutes, just a bit longer than a day on Earth. Your goal is to keep the crew safe until the end.
manual.oxygen.title: Oxygen
manual.oxygen.text: Mars air is almost all carbon dioxide (CO2): nobody can breathe it. MOXIE, a device that traveled inside the Perseverance rover, showed that this CO2 can be turned into oxygen. In the simulation, bring CO2 to the factory to make oxygen.
manual.food.title: Food
manual.food.text: The crew has to eat every day. On the Space Station, NASA's Veggie project grew lettuce in space, and the astronauts ate it! In the simulation, water the greenhouse plants to get food.
manual.shield.title: Shield
manual.shield.text: On Earth, the magnetic field and the air protect us from space radiation. Mars has almost no magnetic field and very thin air: radiation gets through almost freely and it is harmful to health. Build up the shield wall to protect the crew.
manual.energy.title: Energy
manual.energy.text: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity. Mars is very dusty: when dust covers the panels, light can't reach them and they make less energy. Clean them often, because every other task uses energy.
manual.crew.title: Crew
manual.crew.text: Teamwork is key! Tap a crew member, then a room, to give them a task (manual mode). On AUTO they decide alone and go to the lowest bar, but they don't always pick the best. At first they work slower than you.
manual.rover.title: Rover
manual.rover.text: A rover is a robot vehicle that explores Mars. The first one was Sojourner, in 1997. Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater in 2021 to collect rock samples. In the simulation, the rover collects samples and uses energy while the base keeps running.
manual.events.title: Events
manual.events.text: Every sol brings something: dust storms that cover the panels, solar storms with more radiation or mold in the greenhouse. There are good surprises too! Watch the alerts, check the bars and choose what to fix first.
manual.messages.title: Messages
manual.messages.text: Earth sends you warnings so you can get ready. But Mars is so far away that the signal takes several minutes to arrive, so some warnings arrive when the problem has already started. Read them, but also watch what happens in the base.
manual.ready.title: All set!
manual.ready.text: All four bars go down over time. If one reaches zero, the crew has to evacuate and the mission ends. Look after all four, coordinate your crew and watch the alerts!
minigame.greenhouse.introTitle: How do you grow food in space?
minigame.greenhouse.guide1: Mars soil is toxic for plants: we use soil brought from Earth.
minigame.greenhouse.guide2: Each plant needs water and LED light. See what it asks for and bring the tool.
minigame.greenhouse.guide3: Plants take CO₂ from the air and give off O₂. Food and air!
minigame.shield-wall.introTitle: Why does Mars need a shield?
minigame.shield-wall.guide1: Earth has a magnetic shield that stops radiation. Mars lost it: radiation reaches the ground!
minigame.shield-wall.guide2: Water and Mars soil (regolith) stop radiation. Plug the holes in the wall!
minigame.shield-wall.guide3: The Curiosity rover measures it with its RAD meter. Don't let it fill up!
rover.introTitle: How does Perseverance store its samples?
rover.guide1: Catch rocks and dodge the soft sand: the Spirit rover got stuck in it!
rover.guide2: Hold the drill down: it cuts a rock core, a bit thicker than a pencil.
rover.guide3: Put it in the tube and seal it, so nothing from outside gets in.
rover.guide4: The tube goes on the shelf. Perseverance carries 43 tubes!
rover.tubeInstruction: Put the rock in the tube and tap it to seal it!
rover.fact: Perseverance carries 43 tubes, and each sample is the size of a piece of chalk.
